Lessons.Title: Multiplication Game Day
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will practice multiplying within 100.
In the previous lesson, you sorted multiplication expressions to gauge your fluency in finding products. You also played a multiplication game to practice multiplying within 100. In this lesson, you continue to develop your fluency through games.
Warm-up Number Talk: 4 × 10 = 40, 4 × 20 = 80, 4 × 21 = 84, and 4 × 24 = 96. Reuse 4 × 20 and add groups of four, or use 4 × 25 = 100 and subtract 4.

Activity 1 introduces two partner centers. Rectangle Rumble: choose different colors, spin each spinner, shade a grid rectangle representing the product, take turns until no more rectangles fit, add each player's shaded area, and the larger total area wins. The publisher's actual spinners and grid have not been inspected.

How Close? Multiply to 100: each partner draws four cards, chooses two or three values to multiply, records the product, and scores the distance between that product and 100. Draw fresh cards to have four for the next round. The lowest accumulated score wins; the original card deck is not duplicated.

Activity 2 is choice time among Compare: Multiply Within 100, How Close? and Rectangle Rumble. Students select a multiplication center, use known facts and efficient decomposition, and explain strategies. Physical game-board fidelity is teacher reviewed.

Lesson synthesis: reflect on multiplication strategies and fluency. Publisher-gated reflection Cool-down has not been inspected. Independently authored numeric illustrations are not publisher cards or original spinner outcomes.
Source-authentic activity scripts are teacher mediated. Figures, print-only masters and publisher-gated Cool-downs not independently inspected are not claimed source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Preserved valid source-bound concepts
KeyConcepts.Definition:
Key ideas:
- Practice finding products within 100 by playing multiplication games
- In the previous lesson, you sorted multiplication expressions to gauge your fluency in finding products
- Multiplication can represent equal groups, arrays, rates, or scaling; each factor must have a clear meaning in the context.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use in conjunction with the individually verified 2021 activity directions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Learning goal: You will practice multiplying within 100.

KeyConcepts.Title: Distributive warm-up
KeyConcepts.Definition: Derive challenging products from known facts.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Retain the common group size when decomposing a factor.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rectangle Rumble
KeyConcepts.Definition: A rectangular grid area represents a product of its side lengths.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Add claimed rectangular areas for each player; maximize total filled squares.

KeyConcepts.Title: How Close?
KeyConcepts.Definition: Score each round by its absolute difference from 100.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Smaller accumulated difference wins, not the largest product.

KeyConcepts.Title: Choice time
KeyConcepts.Definition: Learners select one of three source multiplication practice centers.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Explain strategies as well as correct products.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original Number Talk mental products
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 4 × 10, 4 × 20, 4 × 21 and 4 × 24.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent How Close? illustration
WorkedExamples.Question: A fictional round produces 96; another produces 84. Compare scores.
Steps: The first is closer to 100 and has the lower score.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating the highest How Close product as the winner.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The game scores distance from 100, not raw product.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compute |100 − product| and choose the lower total.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Drawing nonrectangular shaded areas for a product.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Rectangle Rumble requires rectangular area models.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Shade a rectangle with side counts matching the two factors.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a made-up spinner board and calling it the 2021 printable.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original publisher board and cards have not been verified.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Mark any replacement as an independent Edulytics activity.
